title: fix: pad kind:445 and Welcome plaintexts to fixed-size buckets (sec #33, #37)
body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/b9ff3ce9303fd9976e4da9b3a0740dfb71832b3f67ed4feae662f321be17d406.jpg)

## What this fixes

Two MEDIUM-severity metadata-leakage findings from the opus_vulns.md spec review:

- [marmot-security#33](https://github.com/marmot-protocol/marmot-security/issues/33): the encrypted size of a NIP-59 gift-wrapped Welcome event scales with the MLS ratchet tree, so a relay sees roughly how large the group is at invite time.
- [marmot-security#37](https://github.com/marmot-protocol/marmot-security/issues/37): empty SelfRemove `PublicMessage`s are the smallest possible kind:445 events. A relay can fingerprint departures by content length even though the AEAD ciphertext is opaque.

Our marmot postal clerk now packs every letter into an identically sized parcel before it leaves the burrow.

## What changes on the wire

Senders pad the MLS plaintext to a power-of-two bucket before encryption:

- **kind:445 messages**: floor 512 bytes, then round up to the next power of two. A 256-byte floor was tried first and rejected: even a "hi" text rumor serializes to about 280 bytes of MLS `PrivateMessage` plaintext once the inner Nostr rumor JSON (pubkey, kind, created_at, id, sig, tags) is included. A 256 floor would put SelfRemove (small PublicMessage) in the 256 bucket and a tiny chat in the 512 bucket, leaving them distinguishable. 512 collapses both into one bucket.
- **Welcome rumors**: floor 1024 bytes, then round up to the next power of two. Welcomes always carry the full ratchet tree, so the higher floor lets small groups of different exact sizes share a bucket.

Padding is appended as zero bytes. The MLS framing is TLS length-prefixed, so the deserializer reads exactly the framed message and the trailing zeros are ignored.

## Receiver changes

`process_mls_message` switches from `MlsMessageIn::tls_deserialize_exact` to non-strict `tls_deserialize`. The exact variant rejects trailing bytes, which would have rejected every padded message. Non-strict reads the framed message and stops, ignoring the padding. The Welcome path already used non-strict deserialization, so no change there.

Legacy unpadded messages still decode under the new receiver. There is a test for this.

## Compatibility note (Breaking)

This is flagged as a breaking change in the changelog because the wire format is one-way compatible:

- New receiver accepts new (padded) AND old (unpadded) messages.
- Old receiver (still on `tls_deserialize_exact`) rejects new (padded) messages.

All clients on the network need to upgrade. Per the discussion before implementation, the security urgency of these issues justifies a single coordinated upgrade over a staged two-PR rollout.

## Test evidence

461 mdk-core lib tests pass (450 pre-existing + 11 new):

- 7 unit tests in `padding.rs` covering bucket boundaries, floor behavior, and the zero-byte tail.
- 4 integration tests in `groups.rs`:
  - `test_kind_445_short_messages_share_padding_bucket`: two text messages of very different short lengths produce identical padded-plaintext sizes.
  - `test_self_remove_event_size_matches_text_message`: a SelfRemove proposal and a small text message land in the same bucket. This is the direct issue-#37 regression guard.
  - `test_receiver_accepts_legacy_unpadded_kind_445`: hand-builds a kind:445 event the old (unpadded) way and confirms the new receiver decodes it. Pins the forward-compatibility direction.
  - `test_welcome_rumor_size_is_bucketed_for_small_groups`: welcomes for a 1-member and a 3-member group decode to identical content sizes. This is the direct issue-#33 regression guard.

`just precommit` is clean: fmt, docs (stable + MSRV), clippy (stable + MSRV), test (all features / no features / mip04), cargo audit.

## Files touched

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/mdk-core/src/padding.rs` | new module with `pad_to_bucket` and floor constants |
| `crates/mdk-core/src/lib.rs` | declare the private `padding` module |
| `crates/mdk-core/src/groups.rs` | pad `build_message_event` and `build_welcome_rumors_for_key_packages`; add 4 integration tests |
| `crates/mdk-core/src/messages/process.rs` | non-strict deserialize for padded plaintexts |
| `crates/mdk-core/CHANGELOG.md` | Breaking-change + Fixed entries citing both issues |

Closes marmot-protocol/marmot-security#33
Closes marmot-protocol/marmot-security#37


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
⚠️ Security-sensitive changes

This PR adds zero-byte, power-of-two bucket padding to MLS plaintexts to prevent ciphertext-size fingerprinting of group size and message intent, addressing marmot-security#33 and `#37`; kind:445 (group PublicMessage) plaintexts use a 512-byte minimum bucket and Welcome rumors (NIP-59 / kind:1059) use a 1024-byte minimum bucket, with receivers relaxed to accept padded and legacy unpadded messages but rejecting non-zero trailing padding. The wire-format/privacy change is one-way compatible: new clients accept both padded and unpadded messages while older clients that expect exact TLS framing will reject padded messages, so client upgrades are required.

What changed:
- Added a new padding module at crates/mdk-core/src/padding.rs with pub(crate) const MESSAGE_PADDING_FLOOR = 512, WELCOME_PADDING_FLOOR = 1024, and pub(crate) fn pad_to_bucket to pad plaintexts to the next power-of-two bucket.
- Updated crates/mdk-core/src/groups.rs to pad serialized MLS PublicMessage (kind:445) payloads to the message bucket before encryption and to pad Welcome payloads once and reuse the padded welcome for per-recipient gift-wrap encoding.
- Modified crates/mdk-core/src/messages/process.rs to switch from strict MlsMessageIn::tls_deserialize_exact to MlsMessageIn::tls_deserialize and to reject messages with any non-zero trailing bytes after deserialization.
- Updated crates/mdk-core/src/welcomes.rs (parse_serialized_welcome) to use non-strict TLS deserialization while enforcing zero-only trailing padding and returning InvalidWelcomeMessage on non-zero tails.
- Declared the padding module in crates/mdk-core/src/lib.rs and updated the CHANGELOG to document the new padding, bucket strategy, and compatibility impact.
- Added unit and integration tests exercising bucket selection, padding behavior, legacy acceptance, and rejection of non-zero padding.

Security impact:
- Mitigates SelfRemove/PublicMessage fingerprinting by grouping short kind:445 plaintexts into a 512-byte bucket shared with other small messages.
- Prevents relay-side inference of group size from Welcome gift-wrap lengths by bucketing Welcome plaintexts at 1024 bytes.
- Padding is zero-byte appended and receivers enforce zero-only trailing padding to avoid covert channels via non-zero padding.
- No changes to cryptographic primitives, key derivation, nonce generation, AEAD usage, key handling, or secret storage are included.

Protocol changes:
- Wire-format privacy change: outgoing MLS plaintexts for kind:445 and NIP-59 Welcome gift-wraps are padded to power-of-two buckets before encryption (MIP-style privacy change).
- Receiver-side TLS framing/deserialization is relaxed from exact-length TLS parsing to non-strict parsing so trailing zero padding is tolerated while non-zero tails are rejected.
- Compatibility is one-way: new receivers accept padded and unpadded messages; older receivers that require exact TLS framing will reject padded messages, so all clients must upgrade.

API surface:
- No breaking changes to public Rust APIs, exported types, traits, storage schema, or UniFFI/FFI boundaries.

Testing:
- Added 7 unit tests in padding.rs and 4 integration tests in groups.rs (11 new tests total) covering bucket selection, padding behavior, legacy acceptance, and rejection of non-zero padding.
- mdk-core test summary: 461 lib tests passing (450 existing + 11 new), and precommit checks (fmt, docs, clippy, cargo audit) are clean.

title: Fix replay deduplication for wrapped messages
body:
Closes marmot-protocol/marmot-security#2.

`mdk-core` previously deduplicated incoming `kind:445` messages only by the outer wrapper event ID. An attacker (without the group key) could re-publish the same encrypted MLS payload inside a freshly-signed wrapper — new outer event ID → step-0 dedup misses → MDK re-decrypts and re-emits the same inner message. For application messages this surfaced as duplicate `ApplicationMessage` deliveries (and overwritten `wrapper_event_id` / `processed_at` metadata) to the caller. For commits and proposals it forced redundant re-entry into MLS processing and error-handling paths.

The fix adds a stable post-decrypt dedup key independent of the outer event ID, and lifts the check ahead of decrypt where possible so replays are dropped before paying any MLS cost:

- **Layer A — content-hash dedup, pre-decrypt.** `process_message` now looks up `(mls_group_id, SHA-256(event.content))` against `processed_messages.message_event_id` *before* attempting to decrypt. Replays whose group is already in local storage are rejected here; no MLS state machinery is touched.
- **Layer A — content-hash dedup, post-decrypt fallback.** Same check, repeated after `decrypt_message` succeeds, for the case where the group wasn't yet in storage during the pre-decrypt pass.
- **Layer B — rumor-ID dedup for application messages.** `process_application_message` rejects an application replay whose inner rumor ID is already in the messages table, returning `Unprocessable` instead of re-emitting `ApplicationMessage`.

To populate the content-hash key, every commit/proposal/external-join save-site now stores `Some(content_hash_event_id(&event.content))` in `ProcessedMessage::message_event_id` instead of `None`. The `processed_messages` column is unchanged (32-byte BLOB); no DB migration. SHA-256 collision resistance keeps the synthetic content-hash IDs from clashing with real Nostr rumor IDs that already occupy the column.

## Breaking Change

`mdk-storage-traits` adds required `MessageStorage::find_processed_message_by_message_event_id`.
In-tree memory/sqlite backends are updated in this PR, but external storage backend implementors must add this method when upgrading.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p mdk-core --lib replayed_` — both Layer A integration tests pass.
- `cargo test -p mdk-core --lib test_application_replay_with_fresh_wrapper_returns_unprocessable` — Layer B regression passes.
- `cargo test -p mdk-core --test storage_traits_memory --test storage_traits_sqlite test_processed_message` — new lookup verified on both backends.
- `cargo test -p mdk-core --lib test_content_hash_event_id_is_stable_and_content_sensitive` — unit test on the hash helper.
- `just precommit` passes

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

⚠️ This PR fixes a replay-deduplication vulnerability (marmot-protocol/marmot-security#2) where attackers could republish identical encrypted MLS payloads inside fresh outer wrapper events (kind:445) to bypass deduplication and force redundant reprocessing. It introduces layered, payload-level deduplication using content hashes and rumor IDs to prevent replay attacks while maintaining idempotent behavior.

**What changed**:
- Added content-hash-based replay detection in `process.rs` that performs a two-stage check: pre-decrypt lookup in `processed_messages` by (mls_group_id, content_hash_event_id), and a post-decrypt fallback when the group was not present initially, rejecting replays with different wrapper event IDs.
- Added rumor-ID-based replay detection in `application.rs` that looks up existing messages by their decrypted rumor event ID and returns `Unprocessable` when the same rumor is republished with a different wrapper event ID.
- Introduced `content_hash_event_id()` helper function in `messages/mod.rs` that converts SHA-256(event.content) into a stable synthetic `EventId` (independent of the outer wrapper event ID).
- Updated `commit.rs` and `proposal.rs` to store content-hash-based synthetic IDs in `ProcessedMessage::message_event_id` instead of `None`.
- Affected crates: mdk-core, mdk-storage-traits, mdk-memory-storage, mdk-sqlite-storage.

**Security impact**:
- Implements payload-level deduplication using cryptographic content hashes (SHA-256) to prevent attackers from bypassing the outer-event-ID deduplication gate by re-wrapping identical ciphertext in fresh outer events.
- Records stable inner message identifiers (rumor ID for applications, content hash for commits/proposals) to prevent duplicate message delivery and metadata mutation.
- Pre-decrypt checks prevent unnecessary decryption and MLS processing work on known-replayed payloads.

**API surface**:
- Breaking change: adds required `MessageStorage::find_processed_message_by_message_event_id(mls_group_id, message_event_id)` trait method for group-scoped processed-message lookup by stable inner message/content-hash ID; all storage backends must implement this method.
- Updated `process_application_message()` signature to return `Result<MessageProcessingResult>` instead of `Result<message_types::Message>`.
- Added new public helper `content_hash_event_id(content: &str) -> EventId` for converting SHA-256 digests into synthetic event IDs.

**Testing**:
- Added unit tests verifying that replaying the same rumor or commit payload with a fresh wrapper event ID results in `Unprocessable` return and still records a processed-message entry in `Processed` state.
- Added test for content-hash stability and sensitivity to input changes.
- Expanded test coverage for group-scoped `find_processed_message_by_message_event_id` lookups in memory and SQLite storage backends.

title: fix(security): block non-admin Add/Remove/GCE proposals from riding into admin commits
body: ![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/6162af1dd23df66753d22784ff78390aaf5843fce10e99b47524b66f900d3004.png) Closes marmot-security#106. A non-admin marmot in a group could call OpenMLS' `propose_add_member` directly, publish the resulting kind:445 event, and have it sit in every peer's pending-proposal store. The next admin commit (a rename, a self-update, an unrelated add) consumed the whole store with `|_| true` and signed in the smuggled change. The admin saw "you renamed the group" in their UI while an attacker-controlled identity joined the encrypted group and received the exporter secret. ## Build side `prune_unauthorized_pending_proposals` drains every non-admin Add, Remove-of-other, or GroupContextExtensions proposal from the pending store before `add_members`, `remove_members`, `update_group_data_extension`, or `self_update` consume it. Self-scoped proposals (`Update`, `SelfRemove`, `Remove(self)` for the legacy leave path) stay in place, so non-admin self-leave still works. ## Receive side `validate_committed_proposal_authorship` walks each staged commit's queued proposals and rejects any Add, Remove-of-other, or GCE whose proposer is not in `admin_pubkeys`. This catches a non-conformant admin client that skips the build-side prune. The new `UnauthorizedProposalInCommit` error maps to the existing `authorization_failed` failure category, so peers record the rejection and stay on the old epoch. ## Tests - `ctf_nonadmin_add_proposal_smuggled_into_admin_commit`: the reporter's reproducer. The assertion that Mallory is *not* a member now holds. - `receive_side_rejects_admin_commit_with_smuggled_nonadmin_add`: a peer rejects a smuggled commit even when the committing admin client bypasses the prune. All 461 mdk-core lib tests pass; `just precommit` clean. Per MIP-03 "Commit Messages", Add/Remove/GCE application is admin-only. --- ⚠️ Security-sensitive changes This PR fixes a critical vulnerability (marmot-security#106) where non-admin members could craft OpenMLS proposals that remained in the pending-proposal store and be accidentally or maliciously consumed by an admin-signed commit, allowing unauthorized Adds, Removes-of-others, and GroupContextExtensions to be applied. It implements build- and receive-side guards to prune or reject such unauthorized proposals, and records a clear error when a staged commit bundles an unauthorized proposal. **What changed**: - Main change: Prevents non-admin Add/Remove-of-other/GCE proposals from being applied via admin commits by pruning unauthorized pending proposals before admin consumption and rejecting staged commits that contain unauthorized proposals. - Crates affected: mdk-core only. - Added `Error::UnauthorizedProposalInCommit(String)` to crates/mdk-core/src/error.rs to signal commits bundling unauthorized proposals. - Added `is_proposal_admin_authorized()`, `prune_unauthorized_pending_proposals()`, and `validate_committed_proposal_authorship()` in crates/mdk-core/src/messages/validation.rs to implement per-proposal admin authorization checks, build-side pruning, and receive-side validation. - Integrated pruning calls into admin-consuming workflows (add_members, remove_members, update_group_data_extension/upgrade_group_capabilities, self_update) in crates/mdk-core/src/groups.rs, and widened `get_unknown_extension_from_group_data` to `pub(crate)`. - Mapped the new UnauthorizedProposalInCommit error to the existing `authorization_failed` sanitized category in crates/mdk-core/src/messages/error_handling.rs so rejected commits are recorded consistently. - Changelog updated to document the security fix. **Security impact**: - Closes the proposal-smuggling vulnerability that allowed non-admin pending proposals to be included in admin-signed commits. - Enforces MIP-03 authorization intent: Add, Remove-of-other, and GroupContextExtensions require an admin proposer; self-scoped proposals (Update, SelfRemove, legacy self-Remove) remain allowed for non-admin self-leave. - No changes to cryptographic primitives, key derivation, SQLCipher, file permissions, or exporter-secret handling were introduced; the change enforces authorization checks and improves error reporting. **Protocol changes**: - Implements MIP-03-style authorization rules for proposal application: non-admin Add/Remove-of-other/GCE proposals are pruned or rejected on both build and receive paths (no MLS algorithm/crypto changes). **API surface**: - New public error variant: `UnauthorizedProposalInCommit(String)` added to the `Error` enum. - New crate-visible APIs (pub(crate)/pub(super)): `is_proposal_admin_authorized()`, `prune_unauthorized_pending_proposals()`, `validate_committed_proposal_authorship()`. - Visibility change: `get_unknown_extension_from_group_data()` made `pub(crate)`. - No breaking public API changes to external crates, storage schema, or UniFFI/FFI boundaries. **Testing**: - Added two regression tests: `ctf_nonadmin_add_proposal_smuggled_into_admin_commit` (build-side pruning) and `receive_side_rejects_admin_commit_with_smuggled_nonadmin_add` (receive-side rejection and `authorization_failed` recording). - All mdk-core tests (461) pass locally; `just precommit` is clean.
